title: Dallas Fed Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey (Sep 2026 data) — 9:30 a.m. CT / 10:30 ET, the manufacturing survey's D+1 sibling, printing 30 minutes behind two confirmed medium prints
source: EST: TWO independent primaries on dallasfed.org, both read direct 2026-09-15 with a desktop user-agent and quoted VERBATIM from their own markup rather than through a summarizing fetcher. (1) The Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey landing page (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tssos, HTTP 200, 42,451 bytes) carries a table headed `2026 Release Dates` with the column headers `Survey Period` and `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)`, the row `September | Tuesday, Sept. 29`, and the publisher's caveat `The publishing process begins at 9:30 a.m. CT. While we strive to ensure the information is published to our website in a timely manner, we cannot guarantee the exact timing all survey content becomes available online`. (2) STRONGER, and new to this entry: the publisher's own August 2026 report (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tssos/2026/2608, HTTP 200, 66,281 bytes) states in prose `Next release: Sept. 29, 2026` — the date named inside a published document, not only in a forward table. 9:30 a.m. CT = 10:30 ET, and it is a process start rather than a release instant. Filed estimate on ONE ground, and it is a schema gap rather than any doubt about the date: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy scopes `FED:` to the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar and carries no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule, so this class cannot reach `confirmed` however good its primary is (bottleneck #3117, filed 2026-09-15, sibling to #2552 and #3058). Checked 2026-09-15
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-15 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the single prior proposal first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md — proposals/dallas-fed-tssos-2026-09-29.from-dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28.json, now shadowed and inert. THE PROPOSAL'S FRAMING IS CORRECTED ON TWO COUNTS, both from the primaries re-read today. (1) The divergence it filed this row to adjudicate is ALREADY OBSERVED, not pending: both August reports state `Data were collected August 18–26` verbatim, so one field window from one institution already produced services wages +3.1 to 18.8 alongside manufacturing wages −9.7 to 21.1. August answered whether the cooling is sector-specific; September tests only whether it persists. (2) `Cooling hard` is a level-vs-average error — manufacturing wages at 21.1 sit at z +0.05, the 57th percentile of their own 236-month history (mean 20.56; the publisher's stated series average is 21.1, so the print landed exactly ON its average), while services at 18.8 sit at z +0.42, the 72nd percentile, in the 75th consecutive month above average. Neither survey cooled below normal, and in standardized terms services is the hotter of the two. THE ROW STILL EARNS ITS PLACE, for a better reason than the one proposed: the six SOURCED prior September editions (each from its year's August report `Next release:` line — Sept 29 2020, Sept 28 2021, Sept 27 2022, Sept 26 2023, Oct 1 2024, Sept 30 2025) rank a median 79.2nd percentile by |open→close| magnitude against their own trailing-60, against a null of 50 and P(≥5 of 6 ≥72) = 0.0079 — and the calendar does NOT explain it (Sep 26–30 window median 55.8, penultimate-September session 49.2, unconditional 50.0). All six carried a LARGER 10:00 ET print 30 minutes ahead: five are the last Tuesday of September (the Conference Board's Consumer Confidence slot) and the sixth, 2024-10-01, is ISM Manufacturing's first-business-day slot. So the magnitude is real, it is someone else's, and 2026-09-29 reproduces the configuration with two confirmed `medium` prints at 10:00 (consumer-confidence-2026-09-29, jolts-2026-09-29) plus FHFA HPI and Case-Shiller at 9:00. This is the 12-01 shape (attribution impossible in principle), not 12-29's clean cordon — and banking the trap in advance is the point, because a later session comparing 79th-percentile September sessions to December's null 46.7 would retrofit a survey story onto a Consumer Confidence artifact. Two facts specific to this edition: the field window derives to Tue Sep 15 → Wed Sep 23 and is SOURCED by 2020's own September report (`September 15–23` verbatim, the exact calendar twin — same August 18–26 window, same Sept 29 release, same Oct 27 follow-on), so it opened the day this research was written and the print contains no observation yet; and it straddles the fomc-2026-09-16 decision (`confirmed`, ~87–91% priced for a 25bp hike), splitting the panel by a policy event mid-collection. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, `low` impact, `estimate` date. Full workup: docs/research/events/dallas-fed-tssos-2026-09-29.md
